minutes.headline: Finance Committee backed deferring capital, new positions and some spending to a fall Special Town Meeting, leaving a surplus.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed the revised FY21 plan: the capital plan was cut back and new positions deferred to a fall special town meeting pending revenue. It discussed level-funded local receipts, pavement management and the OPEB deposit, the budget calendar, and Monty Tech and the Student Opportunity Act. The town manager also reported on a COVID-19 emergency spending request. No budget vote was taken; the meeting adjourned by roll call.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee reviewed a revised FY21 plan that cuts back the capital plan and defers new positions to a fall special town meeting, pending revenue.
Level-funding revenues and reducing new growth leaves a surplus cushion until the fall; no budget vote was taken.
Members debated deferring the pavement management increase, and one proposed deferring the OPEB deposit to November; the town manager preferred the stabilization fund, pending advice.
A member said Lunenburg's Monty Tech assessment rises by more than the Monty Tech budget increase.
The superintendent will be invited to the April 30 meeting, and the meeting adjourned by roll call.

why_it_matters: Capital projects and new positions pushed to a fall special town meeting mean residents may be asked to vote on them later, once revenue is clearer.
The surplus is a cushion against falling state aid and local receipts, so a larger drop than assumed could reduce it and affect next year's tax bill and services.
watch_next: April 30 meeting: debt, sewer and general government, with the school superintendent invited after the school committee budget meeting.
The town manager's check with the financial advisor on the OPEB deposit and stabilization fund.
